brief:
Philippine authorities have stopped investigating extrajudicial killings from the "war on drugs" campaign since former President Rodrigo Duterte's case was transferred to the International Criminal Court, Human Rights Watch reported. The ICC trial, scheduled to begin November 30, 2026, charges Duterte with crimes against humanity in The Hague.

The stalled domestic investigations leave thousands of killings from Duterte's drug campaign unexamined at the national level. His prosecution at the ICC proceeded after the Philippines' withdrawal from the court and lack of credible local accountability.
dek: Philippine authorities have failed to investigate extrajudicial killings in the “war on drugs” since former President Rodrigo Duterte was transferred to the International Criminal Court for prosecution, Human Rights Watch said today. The ICC trial in The Hague against Duterte for crimes against humanity is scheduled to begin on November 30, 2026.
title: Philippine authorities halt drug-war killing investigations as Duterte faces ICC trial
